content:
More than 34 tons of food have been collected so far in Nuevo Laredo through Cáritas de Nuevo Laredo's food drive “Alimenta, Multipliquemos el Milagro por un México sin Hambre,” according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo. The newspaper describes the collection as a historic outpouring of solidarity on the border.

The drive began October 17 and runs through November 15, so donations are still being accepted. Support has come from the community, businesses, shopping centers, schools and individual citizens, with joint collection actions involving Hambre Cero, H-E-B and Mi Tienda, according to the report.

The food goes to vulnerable families in Nuevo Laredo, as well as institutions such as addiction-care centers and children's homes. Aid is distributed weekly, every two weeks or monthly, and between 30 and 40 people a day come seeking basic food items, the report says.

Father Rogelio Lozano Alcorta, president of Cáritas de Nuevo Laredo's board, and Elda Elizondo de Ramos, its director, spoke about the drive, with organizers aiming to substantially expand the aid as the campaign continues toward its November 15 close.

What to watch next: the final total when the drive closes November 15 — and how far the collected food stretches for the families and institutions counting on it.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Milagro de solidaridad en la frontera; Cáritas de Nuevo Laredo logra histórico acopio de víveres," October 29, 2026

title: Cáritas de Nuevo Laredo collects more than 34 tons of food for families in need
